Answer: C
Reason: The CT images demonstrate massive, diffuse dilation of the trachea and main bronchi accompanied by multiple large intrapulmonary cysts/cavities, which are the pathognomonic radiological features of Mounier-Kuhn syndrome (tracheobronchomegaly). The "hilar opacity" noted on the chest X-ray corresponds to these markedly dilated, fluid-filled central airways rather than a mass or lymphadenopathy.
